In the Tang Dynasty, people widely consumed fermented dairy products such as cheese, which was thickened from the milk of cows, sheep, or horses. With further refinement, these products were transformed into two distinct forms: curd and the finest essence. The poet Bai Juyi described this culinary craft in his poem Rising Late.
